headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk from EMQX’s broad network egress paired with godot_rl_agents’ local-only, non-networked runtime.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: EMQX has broad network egress and HTTP API surfaces, so it can ingest externally supplied content; godot_rl_agents has no documented input bridge or shared channel. No default direct parsing path between them is shown, so only an unusual manual bridge would enable injection.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies EMQX output into godot_rl_agents prompts or configs, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between the two, attacker-controlled content can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable any manual copy-paste bridge for untrusted text.
Add a simple allowlist for fields passed from EMQX to godot_rl_agents.
Use read-only exports instead of raw logs.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on any shared messages.

B_data_leakage.rationale: EMQX touches IoT data and has broad network egress, so sensitive telemetry can leave its boundary. godot_rl_agents has no documented data classes or egress, but if it receives EMQX outputs through a shared workspace or API, leakage can extend to multiple work products in default-like setups.
conditions: IF EMQX outputs are written to a shared workspace readable by godot_rl_agents, leakage is possible.
IF godot_rl_agents is extended to ingest EMQX logs or transcripts, those contents can be exposed in downstream outputs.
mitigations: Store EMQX outputs in a separate directory.
Redact IoT identifiers before handoff.
Turn off any automatic export of EMQX logs.
Review file permissions on the shared host.
requires-engineering: add per-agent access controls and audit logs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: EMQX exposes HTTP API and broad network egress, while godot_rl_agents shows no write or network capabilities. The profiles do not show overlapping mutable resources or shared locks, so a write-write conflict is not evidenced; uncertainty stays low because the missing surfaces are explicit.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory or database, conflicts become plausible.
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable state without locking, concurrent updates can race.
mitigations: Keep mutable state owned by one agent only.
Avoid shared write directories.
Run one agent at a time for stateful tasks.
Document which agent may write which resource.
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared store.

D_cascading_error.rationale: EMQX can emit networked outputs, but godot_rl_agents has no documented downstream action-taking authority or parser that treats EMQX output as authoritative. Without a verified handoff, the cascade is not default; the main risk is a manual pipeline that bypasses validation.
conditions: IF EMQX output is fed directly into godot_rl_agents as ground truth, cascading error becomes plausible.
IF a downstream controller acts on godot_rl_agents outputs without verification, errors can propagate.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents.
Require schema validation on all handoffs.
Compare EMQX outputs against a second source.
Log rejected or malformed messages.
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds before any automated action.

E_compliance.rationale: EMQX touches IoT data and may process regulated telemetry, while godot_rl_agents shows no data classes or residency constraints. No explicit mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to any future transfer of regulated IoT data into the game-playing agent.
conditions: IF regulated IoT data is routed from EMQX into godot_rl_agents, policy mismatch may arise.
IF retention or residency rules differ between the two deployments, compliance gaps can appear.
mitigations: Do not route regulated data into godot_rl_agents.
Strip personal or device identifiers before transfer.
Check retention settings on EMQX exports.
Keep a short data-flow note for auditors.
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls across both systems.
